candidate.educational_objective: Apply AAP developmental surveillance, general developmental screening, and autism-screening timing at the 18-month visit.

options.A: Continue developmental surveillance and perform both a standardized general developmental screen and an autism-specific screen during this 18-month visit.
options.B: Perform developmental surveillance only because standardized developmental testing is reserved for children whose caregivers or clinicians report a concern.
options.C: Perform an autism-specific screen but defer the general developmental screen until 24 months because both tools should not be used at the same visit.
options.D: Perform a general developmental screen but defer autism screening until school age unless language regression or repetitive behavior is already present.

candidate.rationale: AAP recommends developmental surveillance at every health-supervision visit, standardized general developmental screening at 9, 18, and 30 months, and autism-specific screening at 18 and 24 months. An 18-month visit therefore includes both standardized screens.
candidate.source_claim_supported: At the 18-month visit, continue developmental surveillance and perform standardized general developmental and autism-specific screening even without parental concerns.
candidate.source_document_title: Developmental Surveillance and Screening Patient Care
candidate.source_locator: Screening schedule — developmental surveillance at every health-supervision visit; standardized general developmental screening at 9, 18, and 30 months; autism screening at 18 and 24 months
candidate.stem: An 18-month-old presents for a routine health-supervision visit. The parent has no specific developmental concerns. Which screening plan best reflects current AAP recommendations?
